## Pharmaceutical and clinical statistics {.title-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Week 10</div>

<div class="concept-line" style="margin-top:1em;">How does statistics enter actual pharmaceutical evidence?</div>

## Today: one evidence chain {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Not another catalog of tests</div><div class="w10-evidence-flow"><div>Populations<span>epidemiology</span></div><b>→</b><div>Patients<span>diagnostics</span></div><b>→</b><div>Interventions<span>clinical trials</span></div><b>→</b><div>Exposure<span>toxicology</span></div><b>→</b><div>Knowledge<span>meta-analysis</span></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">The question and study design determine the interpretation; statistical machinery quantifies <strong>effects and uncertainty</strong>.</div>

## First: can we intervene? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Return to Week 03 · study design</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Observe</div><div class="w10-card-large">Exposure is not allocated</div><div class="w10-card-small">Cohort / case–control / cross-sectional studies</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Randomize</div><div class="w10-card-large">Exposure is allocated</div><div class="w10-card-small">Controlled trial with prespecified endpoints</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Both designs have sampling variability. Random allocation helps break systematic links between measured <em>and unmeasured</em> baseline confounders on average.</p></div>

## Prevalence: how many are affected now? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Disease burden · stock of existing cases</div><div class="w10-bigmath">$\mathrm{Prevalence}=\dfrac{\text{existing cases}}{\text{population at time / period}}$</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Illustrative population</div><div class="w10-card-large">1,000 people</div><div class="w10-card-small">Observed at the start of the year</div></div><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Already affected</div><div class="w10-card-large">50 people</div><div class="w10-card-small">Point prevalence = 50 / 1,000 = 5%</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Prevalence describes population burden. It reflects both arrival of new cases and how long people remain cases.</p></div>

## Incidence: how many become affected? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">New events among people initially at risk</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:10.5em;"><img src="figures/incidence_prevalence.svg" alt="Synthetic population illustrates prevalence and new cases over a period"></div><div class="w10-equation">$\text{Cumulative incidence}=40/950\approx4.2\%$ during 1 year</div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Cumulative incidence is a risk over a specified time horizon, assuming appropriate follow-up and accounting for censoring when needed.</p></div>

## Incidence rate uses person-time {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">A different denominator and unit</div><div class="w10-bigmath">$\text{Incidence rate}=\dfrac{\text{new cases}}{\sum\text{person-time at risk}}$</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Example</div><div class="w10-card-large">40 new cases</div><div class="w10-card-small">Among a dynamic followed population</div></div><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Observed time</div><div class="w10-card-large">900 person-years</div><div class="w10-card-small">Different people contribute different durations</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Incidence rate</div><div class="w10-card-large">4.44 / 100 person-years</div><div class="w10-card-small">An event rate, not a 4.44% probability</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Rate and probability become close only under additional conditions, including relatively low risk over the time horizon.</div>

## Revisit the invisible third variable {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Synthetic association · sugary drinks → school performance</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:10.8em;"><img src="figures/confounding_dag1.svg" alt="Causal directed acyclic graph with household resources influencing both sugary drinks and performance"></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Household resources $Z$ can be a <strong>confounder</strong> if it is a common cause of $X$ and $Y$; a mediator or collider would have a different causal role.</div>

## An association that appears when pooled {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Compare within the low- and high-rent strata</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12.6em;display:grid; grid-template-areas:'stack';align-items:center;justify-items:center;"><img src="figures/confounding_strata_masked.svg" alt="Risk of bad school performance within low- and high-rent strata" style="grid-area:stack;z-index:1;max-height:100%;width:auto;"><img src="figures/confounding_strata.svg" class="fragment fade-up" alt="Risk of bad school performance by drink intake within strata and pooled, with exact synthetic counts" style="grid-area:stack;z-index:2;max-height:100%;width:auto;"></div><div class="w10-small-note">Low rent: 10/100 versus 2/20 · high rent: 10/20 versus 50/100 · pooled: 20/120 versus 52/120. All counts synthetic.</div>

## Directed acyclic graph {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Causal interpretation · Stratification blocks the backdoor path</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:10.8em;"><img src="figures/confounding_dag2.svg" alt="Causal directed acyclic graph with household resources influencing both sugary drinks and performance 2"></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">When the association vanishes within strata, it suggests $Z$ confounds both variables rather than $X$ directly causing $Y$—provided no unmeasured confounders remain.</div>

## Confounder or effect modifier? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Two different scientific questions</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3; font-size: 120%"><div class="w10-th">Concept</div><div class="w10-th">What happens?</div><div class="w10-th">What should we do?</div><div>Confounding</div><div>An overall estimate is distorted by differing group compositions</div><div>Adjustment aims at an association net of the confounding pathway</div><div>Effect modification</div><div>Exposure–outcome associations genuinely differ between strata</div><div>Report the strata; an overall effect can conceal clinically useful differences</div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Our synthetic drink example illustrates both:</p><p>$RR$ within low rent $= 2.0$;</p><p>$RR$ within high rent $= 1.33$;</p><p>pooled $RR = 1.0$.</p></div>

## The hospital paradox, once again {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Drug response across three hospitals</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12.6em;"><img src="figures/hospital_simpson.svg" alt="Treatment better at each of three hospitals yet worse after pooling due to differing case mix"></div><div class="w10-small-note">Drug: 30%, 60%, 90% success in hospitals A/B/C; control: 20%, 50%, 80%. Different arm allocations create the pooled reversal.</div>

## When the confounder is measured {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Design and analysis options</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Before data collection</strong><span>Restriction or matching can improve comparability; randomization addresses baseline confounding by design.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>During analysis</strong><span>Stratify, standardize or adjust using regression; always inspect effect modification.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>If effects are broadly common</strong><span>Mantel–Haenszel estimates an adjusted association across strata (with a clear target estimand).</span></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>A common pooled effect is not appropriate when stratum-specific treatment effects differ substantially.</p></div>

## What if confounding is unobserved? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">A fundamental limit of observational evidence</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Propensity methods</div><div class="w10-card-large">Measured covariates</div><div class="w10-card-small">Matching / weighting / adjustment can balance observed confounders</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Sensitivity analysis</div><div class="w10-card-large">Unmeasured covariates</div><div class="w10-card-small">Ask how strong hidden confounding must be to reverse a result</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Triangulate</div><div class="w10-card-large">Different designs</div><div class="w10-card-small">Compare evidence across designs with different weaknesses</div></div></div><div class="warning-box fragment fade-up"><p>These approaches do <strong>not</strong> automatically solve unmeasured confounding; more sophisticated methods are outside this course.</p></div>

## Epidemiology: which effect measure? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Use incidence for risk; distinguish risk from odds</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3; font-size: 120%"><div class="w10-th">Measure</div><div class="w10-th">Formula</div><div class="w10-th">Interpretation</div><div>Risk ($p$)</div><div>Events / people at risk</div><div>Probability over a specified period</div><div>Odds</div><div>$p/(1-p)$</div><div>Event relative to non-event probability</div><div>Relative risk ($RR$)</div><div>$p_\mathrm{T}/p_\mathrm{C}$</div><div>Relative event risk: multiplicative</div><div>Odds ratio ($OR$)</div><div>$[p_\mathrm{T}/(1-p_\mathrm{T})]/[p_\mathrm{C}/(1-p_\mathrm{C})]$</div><div>Multiplicative odds, not risk</div><div>Risk difference ($RD$)</div><div>$p_\mathrm{T}-p_\mathrm{C}$</div><div>Absolute percentage-point difference</div></div><div class="w10-small-note">$\mathrm{T}$ = exposed / treated; $\mathrm{C}$ = comparator. Choose a time horizon and clear event definition.</div>

## Same RR, very different absolute impact {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Why baseline risk matters</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12.4em;"><img src="figures/relative_absolute_risk.svg" alt="Two treatment examples have same relative risk but very different absolute risk differences"></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A $50\%$ relative reduction can mean <strong>1</strong> or <strong>20</strong> events prevented per 100 patients, depending on baseline risk.</div>

## Worked example: risk and risk difference {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Synthetic one-year prevention trial</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Comparator risk</div><div class="w10-card-large">20%</div><div class="w10-card-small">20 events per 100 patients</div></div><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Treatment risk</div><div class="w10-card-large">10%</div><div class="w10-card-small">10 events per 100 patients</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">RR</div><div class="w10-card-large">0.50</div><div class="w10-card-small">Half the event risk under treatment</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Absolute RD</div><div class="w10-card-large">10 percentage points</div><div class="w10-card-small">0.10 − 0.20 = −0.10</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Absolute and relative summaries describe the <strong>same contrast</strong>, on different scales.</div>

## NNT and NNH: put consequences on the same page {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Number needed to treat / harm</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Benefit</div><div class="w10-card-large">NNT = 10</div><div class="w10-card-small">ARR = 0.10 → one additional prevented event per 10 treated, on average</div></div><div class="w10-card warning"><div class="w10-card-label">Harm</div><div class="w10-card-large">NNH = 25</div><div class="w10-card-small">Absolute harm increase 0.04 → one additional adverse event per 25 treated, on average</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Specify comparator, population, endpoint and time horizon. NNT does not identify which patient benefits, and comparing NNT/NNH needs clinical weighting of outcomes.</p></div>

## Attributable fractions: causal language needs care {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Illustrative association · exposure raises risk from 10% to 20%</div><div class="w10-formula-pair"><div><strong>Among exposed</strong><span>$AF_E=(RR-1)/RR=50\%$</span><small>Fraction of exposed cases attributed to exposure, if association is causal</small></div><div><strong>In population</strong><span>$PAF=(R_{pop}-R_0)/R_{pop}\approx23\%$</span><small>With 30% exposed: population risk = 13%, baseline risk = 10%</small></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Attributable fractions are <strong>not</strong> causal without assumptions about confounding, timing and intervention effects.</p></div>

## Diagnostic tests {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part II</div>
<div class="section-title">Diagnostic tests can fall for misclassification</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">We now see what to be aware of when diagnosing patients to estimate prevalence.</div>

## Diagnostic tests: from association to classification {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Return to Bayes · Week 01</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Test accuracy</div><div class="w10-card-large">Sensitivity / specificity</div><div class="w10-card-small">How often the test correctly classifies reference-standard outcomes</div></div><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Population context</div><div class="w10-card-large">Prevalence</div><div class="w10-card-small">How common the target condition is in the tested population</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Patient interpretation</div><div class="w10-card-large">PPV / NPV</div><div class="w10-card-small">How likely a result is to indicate disease / health</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Accuracy statistics alone do not tell us how much to trust a <strong>positive</strong> test.</div>

## Start from four patients categories {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Positive / negative test × present / absent condition</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:11.8em;"><img src="figures/confusion_matrix.svg" alt="Two by two diagnostic classification matrix with true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives"></div><div class="w10-equation">$\mathrm{Sensitivity}=TP/(TP+FN)$ &nbsp;&nbsp; $\mathrm{Specificity}=TN/(TN+FP)$</div>

## Interactive lab · thirty diagnostic metrics {.exercise-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Numbers change together · meaning depends on the denominator</div><div class="w10-conf-widget" id="confWidget">
<div class="w10-conf-left">
<div class="w10-mini-title">Edit the patient counts</div>
<div class="w10-count-grid">
<div class="w10-input-cell"><label class="w10-control">TP · sick & positive<input id="cmTP" type="number" min="0" step="1" value="38"></label></div>
<div class="w10-input-cell"><label class="w10-control">FN · sick & negative<input id="cmFN" type="number" min="0" step="1" value="8"></label></div>
<div class="w10-input-cell"><label class="w10-control">FP · healthy & positive<input id="cmFP" type="number" min="0" step="1" value="12"></label></div>
<div class="w10-input-cell"><label class="w10-control">TN · healthy & negative<input id="cmTN" type="number" min="0" step="1" value="142"></label></div>
</div>
<div class="w10-highlight-metrics"><div><span>Sensitivity</span><strong id="cmSensBig">—</strong></div><div><span>Specificity</span><strong id="cmSpecBig">—</strong></div><div><span>PPV</span><strong id="cmPpvBig">—</strong></div><div><span>NPV</span><strong id="cmNpvBig">—</strong></div></div>
<div class="w10-mini-note">Undefined denominators display “—”. Counts must be nonnegative whole numbers.</div>
</div>
<div class="w10-conf-right">
<div class="w10-mini-title">Explore the full diagnostic vocabulary · 5 columns × 6 metrics</div>
<div class="w10-metric-grid" id="cmMetrics"></div>
</div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Focus on sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV; the more advanced metrics are for recognition, not memorization.
:::

## A metric is a question with a denominator {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Read the conditioning, not just the abbreviation</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3"><div class="w10-th">Metric</div><div class="w10-th">Clinical interpretation</div><div class="w10-th">Definition</div><div>Sensitivity / recall</div><div>Of those truly sick, what fraction tests positive?</div><div>$TP/(TP+FN)$</div><div>Specificity</div><div>Of those truly healthy, what fraction tests negative?</div><div>$TN/(TN+FP)$</div><div>PPV</div><div>Of those testing positive, what fraction is sick?</div><div>$TP/(TP+FP)$</div><div>NPV</div><div>Of those testing negative, what fraction is healthy?</div><div>$TN/(TN+FN)$</div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Sensitivity and specificity condition on <em>reference disease status</em>; predictive values condition on the <em>observed test result</em>.</div>

## A diagnostic marker needs a decision threshold {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Last week: a probability model · today: an action</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Measure</strong><span>A continuous biomarker varies across sick and healthy people.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>Classify</strong><span>Choose a cutoff: trade missed cases against false alarms.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>Validate</strong><span>Estimate sensitivity, specificity and calibration in a new relevant population.</span></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>A model threshold that maximizes an in-sample statistic may be too optimistic in new patients.</p></div>

## Interactive lab · threshold and ROC {.exercise-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Synthetic iron-deficiency status · disease reference label known</div><div class="w10-lab" id="rocWidget">
<div class="w10-controls">
<label class="w10-control">Biomarker (synthetic study)<select id="rocMarker"><option value="ferritin">Ferritin · strong separation</option><option value="folate">Folate · weak separation</option></select></label>
<label class="w10-control">Positive if marker ≤ <strong id="rocCutVal">30</strong><input id="rocCut" type="range" min="0" max="110" value="30" step="1"></label>
<div class="w10-micro">Drag the red threshold line on the left plot; the current operating point moves on the ROC.</div>
<div class="w10-two-output"><div class="w10-output"><span>Sensitivity</span><strong id="rocSen">—</strong></div><div class="w10-output"><span>Specificity</span><strong id="rocSpe">—</strong></div><div class="w10-output"><span>AUC · fixed per marker</span><strong id="rocAuc">—</strong></div><div class="w10-output"><span>Youden cutoff (sample)</span><strong id="rocBest">—</strong></div></div>
</div>
<div class="w10-visual"><svg id="rocSvg" class="w10-svg" style="height:14em" viewBox="0 0 900 475" aria-label="Synthetic biomarker dot plot with draggable threshold and corresponding ROC curve"></svg></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Strong/weak marker distributions are explicitly synthetic and not clinical performance claims. Ferritin values decrease in this simulated iron-deficiency dataset; folate is deliberately weak.
:::

## What the ROC curve is showing {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Each cutoff gives ONE point; all cutoffs give ONE curve</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3"><div class="w10-th">Element</div><div class="w10-th">Definition</div><div class="w10-th">Interpretation</div><div>Horizontal axis</div><div>$1-Sp$</div><div>False-positive rate</div><div>Vertical axis</div><div>$Se$</div><div>True-positive rate</div><div>AUC</div><div>Area under the entire ROC</div><div>Discrimination across all cutoffs; does not change when slider moves</div><div>Upper-left corner</div><div>High&nbsp;$Se$, low&nbsp;$FPR$</div><div>Ideal only if clinical costs and prevalence allow</div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Maximum <em>Youden index</em> and shortest distance to the corner are possible cutoff criteria — neither is a universal clinical optimum.</p></div>

## Which error is more costly? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Clinical thresholds encode clinical decisions</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">High sensitivity</div><div class="w10-card-large">Avoid missed disease</div><div class="w10-card-small">Often acceptable to trigger a confirmatory test</div></div><div class="w10-card warning"><div class="w10-card-label">High specificity</div><div class="w10-card-large">Avoid false positives</div><div class="w10-card-small">Important if unnecessary treatment would be risky</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">AUC</div><div class="w10-card-large">Overall ranking performance</div><div class="w10-card-small">AUC alone does not choose a patient-facing threshold</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Select cutoffs with anticipated costs, prevalence, clinical pathway and independent validation in mind.</div>

## Bayes comes back: PPV changes with prevalence {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Illustrative test: sensitivity 90%, specificity 90%</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card warning"><div class="w10-card-label">Prevalence 1%</div><div class="w10-card-large">PPV = 8.3%</div><div class="w10-card-small">Most positives are false positives at very low prevalence</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Prevalence 20%</div><div class="w10-card-large">PPV = 69.2%</div><div class="w10-card-small">Positive result becomes substantially more credible</div></div></div><div class="w10-bigmath">$PPV=\dfrac{Se\times Prev}{Se\times Prev+(1-Sp)(1-Prev)}$</div>

## Diagnostic uncertainty does not stop at the cutoff {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">A test-accuracy estimate comes from a finite study</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Report intervals</strong><span>Sensitivity and specificity have sampling uncertainty; so does AUC.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>Specify reference standard</strong><span>Errors in the disease reference label can bias measured diagnostic accuracy.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>Verify transportability</strong><span>Prevalence, disease spectrum, laboratories and settings may differ.</span></div></div><div class="warning-box fragment fade-up"><p>If thresholds are chosen on the same data used for evaluation, apparent accuracy may be optimistic.</p></div>

## Pooling samples: when fewer tests can suffice {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Group testing · only when assay dilution is acceptable</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:10.3em;"><img src="figures/pooled_testing.svg" alt="Diagram of pooling patient samples and retesting individuals if pool tests positive"></div><div class="w10-equation">Expected tests per person (idealized) $\approx 1/k + 1-(1-p)^k$</div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Valid only under an appropriate pooling protocol and assumptions; lower assay sensitivity after dilution, dependence and prevalence can change whether pooling helps.</p></div>

## Clinical trials {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part III</div>
<div class="section-title">For causal inference use clinical study</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">We now see all the care we have to give for correct planning and execution.</div>

## Clinical trials: what randomization buys us {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Treatment allocation as a planned intervention</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:11.8em;"><img src="figures/trial_design_flow.svg" alt="Flow of eligible participants through concealed randomization into treatment and comparator arms"></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">The target is a <strong>causal contrast</strong> under a clearly specified intervention, endpoint, population and follow-up.</div>

## Write the question before running the test {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Superiority, noninferiority, equivalence</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3; font-size: 120%"><div class="w10-th">Objective</div><div class="w10-th">Clinical question</div><div class="w10-th">Statistical logic</div><div>Superiority</div><div>Is&nbsp;$T$&nbsp;better than&nbsp;$C$?</div><div>Evidence that the effect exceeds a reference such as zero</div><div>Noninferiority</div><div>Is&nbsp;$T$&nbsp;not unacceptably worse?</div><div>One-sided prespecified margin and appropriate CI</div><div>Equivalence</div><div>Are effects close enough in both directions?</div><div>Two-sided margin; TOST / corresponding 90% CI</div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">The same observed treatment difference can support different conclusions depending on the <strong>prespecified question</strong>.</div>

## Every trial needs a defensible comparator {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Ethics and interpretability</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Placebo</div><div class="w10-card-large">When appropriate</div><div class="w10-card-small">Can separate treatment effect from expectations, but ethical constraints apply</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Active comparator</div><div class="w10-card-large">Standard of care</div><div class="w10-card-small">Tests relative benefit or acceptable loss against existing treatment</div></div><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">No intervention</div><div class="w10-card-large">Sometimes relevant</div><div class="w10-card-small">Not interchangeable with placebo when expectations/attention matter</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Comparator choice is part of the scientific and ethical question, not an afterthought.</p></div>

## Endpoints: one convincing outcome beats many weak ones {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Efficacy, safety and multiplicity</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:9.6em;"><img src="figures/trial_endpoints.svg" alt="Prespecified primary, supportive secondary, and safety endpoints on separate cards"></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Define what is measured, when, how and by whom. Multiple confirmatory claims require an error-control strategy.</div>

## Baseline, covariates and missing follow-up {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Prevent avoidable ambiguity</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Before dosing</strong><span>Record baseline endpoint and prognostic factors; plan any covariate adjustment.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>During follow-up</strong><span>Apply identical outcome ascertainment and monitoring principles across arms.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>At analysis</strong><span>Define the population to analyze and the assumptions for missing values before seeing outcomes.</span></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Baseline differences can occur by chance despite proper randomization. Do not use significance testing as a gatekeeper for adjustment.</p></div>

## Masking and allocation concealment {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">These prevent different problems</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Concealment</div><div class="w10-card-large">Before assignment</div><div class="w10-card-small">Prevents knowledge of the upcoming allocation from influencing enrolment</div></div><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Masking</div><div class="w10-card-large">After assignment</div><div class="w10-card-small">Can reduce performance and outcome-assessment biases</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Transparent reporting</div><div class="w10-card-large">Throughout</div><div class="w10-card-small">Specify exactly who was masked and how</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">Labels like “double blind” are less informative than naming <strong>participants, clinicians, assessors and analysts</strong>.</div>

## Randomization: not all methods are interchangeable {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Use transparent, prespecified rules</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3"><div class="w10-th">Design</div><div class="w10-th">What it changes</div><div class="w10-th">What to remember</div><div>Simple random</div><div>Each assignment independent</div><div>Some imbalance is natural, especially in small studies</div><div>Blocked / stratified</div><div>Restrictions preserve balance</div><div>Specify blocks, factors and concealment protocol</div><div>Biased coin</div><div>Preferentially corrects imbalance</div><div>Assignment probability changes using current counts</div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Proper randomization does not guarantee equal arm sizes or eliminate chance variation in prognostic factors.</p></div>

## What goes into sample-size planning? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">You cannot compute $n$ without assumptions</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Clinically important difference</strong><span>Choose $\Delta$ on the original outcome scale, not merely an attainable statistical signal.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>Within-arm SD and α</strong><span>Higher variability or more stringent α generally needs more patients.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>Target power and operations</strong><span>Higher power needs more patients; add credible allowance for attrition and operational limitations.</span></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>The widget gives an illustrative approximation for two independent groups, not a regulatory trial-planning calculation.</p></div>

## Read a trial result as an effect and its interval {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">An example reporting sentence</div><div class="w10-quote">“The treatment reduced systolic blood pressure by an estimated <strong>5 mmHg</strong> relative to control (95% CI <strong>2 to 8 mmHg</strong> reduction), at 12 weeks.”</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Magnitude</div><div class="w10-card-large">5 mmHg</div><div class="w10-card-small">Is it clinically important?</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Uncertainty</div><div class="w10-card-large">95% CI</div><div class="w10-card-small">What range of effects remains compatible with data?</div></div><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Context</div><div class="w10-card-large">12 weeks</div><div class="w10-card-small">Who, when, comparator, adverse effects?</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Statistical significance is not a complete benefit–risk assessment.</p></div>

## Toxicology {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part IV</div>
<div class="section-title">It is actually important to prove safety first</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">We now see the basic idea of assessing drug toxicity.</div>

## Toxicology: dose, effect and harm {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Repeated exposures and nonlinear biological responses</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Pharmacology</div><div class="w10-card-large">EC50 / IC50</div><div class="w10-card-small">Dose or concentration at a defined half-maximal response</div></div><div class="w10-card warning"><div class="w10-card-label">Toxicology</div><div class="w10-card-large">TC50 / LC50</div><div class="w10-card-small">Half-maximal toxic response / 50% lethality in a stated assay</div></div><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Experiment</div><div class="w10-card-large">Doses and times</div><div class="w10-card-small">Exposure schedule and concentration range matter</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A dose–response model describes a particular endpoint under a particular exposure protocol.</div>

## Sigmoids are useful, not universal {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Potency, slope, saturation</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12.2em;"><img src="figures/dose_response_families.svg" alt="Sigmoidal dose-response families with shifts in EC50 and slope changes"></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>The extended logit curve from last week links log-dose with response shape; model choice requires mechanistic and empirical justification.</p></div>

## From Mass Action to the Boltzmann Sigmoid {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">First-principles derivation · Binding kinetics &amp; cooperativity</div>

<div class="w10-three" style="margin-top: 0.4em; gap: 0.7em; align-items: stretch;">
  <!-- Card 1: Mass Action -->
  <div class="w10-card model-border">
  <div class="w10-card-title">1: Equilibrium Mass Action</div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.55em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">
  Receptor $\text{R}$ binds ligand $\text{L}$:
  $$\text{L} + \text{R} \underset{k_{\mathrm{off}}}{\overset{k_{\mathrm{on}}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{RL}, \quad K_{\mathrm{d}} = \frac{[\text{L}][\text{R}]}{[\text{RL}]}$$
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-math" style="font-size: 0.65em;">
  $$\theta = \frac{[\text{RL}]}{[\text{R}]_{\mathrm{tot}}} = \frac{[\text{L}]}{[\text{L}] + K_{\mathrm{d}}}$$
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.4em; margin-top: 0.4em;">
  Hyperbolic response curve on a linear concentration scale ($[\text{L}]$).
  </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Card 2: Log-Dose / Boltzmann Sigmoid -->
  <div class="w10-card estimate-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="w10-card-title">2: Log-Dose reparameterization</div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.55em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">
  Define log-concentration $x = \log[\text{L}]$ and log-dissociation $x_{50} = \log K_{\mathrm{d}}$:
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-math" style="font-size: 0.65em;">
  $$\theta = \frac{e^x}{e^x + e^{x_{50}}} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(x - x_{50})}}$$
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.4em; margin-top: 0.4em;">
  This is <strong>exactly</strong> the standard logistic (Boltzmann) sigmoid on the log-dose axis.
  </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Card 3: Hill Cooperativity -->
  <div class="w10-card uncertainty-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="w10-card-title">3: Hill Cooperativity ($n_{\mathrm{H}}$)</div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.55em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">
  Multi-site binding ($n_{\mathrm{H}}$ molecules bind cooperatively):
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-math" style="font-size: 0.65em;">
  $$\theta = \frac{[\text{L}]^{n_{\mathrm{H}}}}{[\text{L}]^{n_{\mathrm{H}}} + K_{\mathrm{d}}^{n_{\mathrm{H}}}} = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-n_{\mathrm{H}}(x - x_{50})}}$$
  </div>
  <div class="w10-card-sub" style="font-size: 0.4em; margin-top: 0.4em;">
  The Hill coefficient $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ directly scales the <strong>slope factor</strong> (steepness) of the sigmoid.
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="w10-caption fragment fade-up" style="margin-top: 0.75em;"><strong>Mechanistic insight:</strong> The logistic curve is not just an empirical smoothing function—it arises naturally when ligand-receptor equilibrium is plotted against log-concentration. $n_{\mathrm{H}} > 1$ indicates positive cooperativity, while $n_{\mathrm{H}} < 1$ reflects negative cooperativity or multiple receptor subtypes.</div>

## Dose planning determines what can be estimated {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Avoid fitting a curve to the wrong region</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Include a meaningful control</strong><span>Establish baseline or background toxicity.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>Bracket the transition</strong><span>Sample both lower and higher response regions, where feasible; do not require a universal 30–70% range.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>Replicate and account for exposure</strong><span>Dose spacing, sample size, time and measurement error affect certainty.</span></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">An apparent EC50 can be extrapolation if the measured doses never bracket half-response.</div>

## NOAEL / LOAEL versus modeled BMD {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">One comes from dose groups; one from a curve</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12em;"><img src="figures/toxicology_bmd.svg" alt="Illustrative observed dose groups and fitted adverse-effect response with NOAEL LOAEL and benchmark dose"></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>NOAEL/LOAEL are study-dependent observed dose levels. BMD (benchmark dose) is fitted at a specified benchmark response; BMDL is a lower confidence bound for that modeled dose.</p></div>

## Exposure duration changes the interpretation {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">One dose, more than one answer</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Acute</div><div class="w10-card-large">Single/short exposure</div><div class="w10-card-small">Different endpoints than prolonged dosing</div></div><div class="w10-card model"><div class="w10-card-label">Repeated-dose</div><div class="w10-card-large">Weeks/months</div><div class="w10-card-small">Accumulation and adaptation may alter response</div></div><div class="w10-card warning"><div class="w10-card-label">Clinical translation</div><div class="w10-card-large">Species and protocols</div><div class="w10-card-small">Do not equate experimental safety thresholds directly with a safe patient dose</div></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A toxicity statement is incomplete without dose, route, exposure duration, species/population and endpoint.</div>

## Meta-analysis {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part V</div>
<div class="section-title">Human knowledge accumulated</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">Why consensus provides a stronger evidence.</div>

## From individual studies to cumulative evidence {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Systematic review → quantitative synthesis</div><div class="w10-step-stack"><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">01</span><strong>Define a systematic question</strong><span>Population, intervention/exposure, comparator, outcome and study design.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">02</span><strong>Search and appraise</strong><span>Include eligible studies transparently; assess bias and publication/selective reporting.</span></div><div class="w10-step"><span class="w10-num">03</span><strong>Synthesize</strong><span>Combine comparable estimates and examine between-study differences.</span></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A meta-analysis is a calculation <em>inside</em> a systematic review, not a substitute for one.</div>

## How to read a forest plot {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Each line = one study, diamond = pooled estimate</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:13.3em;"><img src="figures/forest_anatomy.svg" alt="Synthetic common-effect forest plot showing individual risk ratios and confidence intervals and green pooled diamond"></div><div class="w10-small-note">Squares represent study estimates; square area reflects precision weight. Horizontal lines are 95% CIs. The dashed line at RR=1 is the no-effect reference.</div>

## Why more precise studies get more weight {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Common-effect model, under its assumptions</div><div class="w10-bigmath">$w_i=1/SE_i^2,\qquad \hat\theta_{pool}=\dfrac{\sum_i w_i\hat\theta_i}{\sum_i w_i}$</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">High precision</div><div class="w10-card-large">Small SE</div><div class="w10-card-small">Larger inverse-variance weight</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Low precision</div><div class="w10-card-large">Large SE</div><div class="w10-card-small">Smaller weight</div></div></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>For ratio measures, average <strong>log risk ratios / log odds ratios</strong>, then exponentiate. Pool only effects on a comparable estimand and scale.</p></div>

## What if studies truly differ? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Between-study heterogeneity</div><div class="w10-table" style="--cols:3; font-size: 120%"><div class="w10-th">Approach</div><div class="w10-th">Concept</div><div class="w10-th">Caution</div><div>Common-effect</div><div>One underlying effect in the included studies</div><div>Variation attributed to sampling uncertainty</div><div>Random-effects</div><div>A distribution of underlying study effects</div><div>Accounts for between-study heterogeneity; requires more assumptions</div><div>Subgroups / sensitivity</div><div>Explore prespecified differences</div><div>Avoid assuming any pooled mean applies to all patients</div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A narrower pooled CI is not evidence that all populations benefit equally.</div>

## Funnel plots: a clue, not a verdict {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Small studies, precision and selective publication</div><div class="w10-figure" style="height:12.3em;"><img src="figures/funnel_anatomy.svg" alt="Side by side approximately symmetric and asymmetric funnel plots with effect size and standard error axes"></div><div class="definition-box fragment fade-up"><p>Asymmetry may result from publication bias, heterogeneity, methodological differences or chance; assess alongside study design and reporting.</p></div>

## One map: where statistics enters evidence {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">From research question to decision</div><div class="w10-summary-flow"><div><strong>Who?</strong><span>Population, prevalence, selection</span></div><div><strong>What?</strong><span>Diagnosis and misclassification</span></div><div><strong>Why?</strong><span>Trial causal effect and benefit–harm</span></div><div><strong>How much?</strong><span>Dose–response and uncertainty</span></div><div><strong>How sure?</strong><span>Systematic review and meta-analysis</span></div></div><div class="concept-line fragment fade-up">A sound interpretation requires <strong>design + estimand + measurement + uncertainty + applicability</strong>.</div>

## Next: the data do not always come one patient at a time {.section-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Week 11 · time, signals, survival and prediction</div><div class="w10-hero">Outcomes may arrive as <strong>trajectories</strong>, <strong>repeated measurements</strong> and <strong>time until an event</strong>.</div><div class="w10-card-grid"><div class="w10-card observed"><div class="w10-card-label">Time series</div><div class="w10-card-large">Signal trajectories</div><div class="w10-card-small">Serial dependence matters</div></div><div class="w10-card uncertainty"><div class="w10-card-label">Survival</div><div class="w10-card-large">Time-to-event</div><div class="w10-card-small">Follow-up and censoring matter</div></div><div class="w10-card estimate"><div class="w10-card-label">Prediction</div><div class="w10-card-large">Generalization</div><div class="w10-card-small">Validation matters</div></div></div>

<!-- One JS block. Do not load week10.js separately. -->
<script>
/* Week 10: one scoped script, initialized once. The QMD embeds this verbatim. */
(function(){
'use strict';
const $=id=>document.getElementById(id);
const clamp=(x,a,b)=>Math.max(a,Math.min(b,x));
const N=(id,fallback)=>{const el=$(id);const v=el?Number(el.value):fallback;return Number.isFinite(v)?v:fallback;};
const out=(id,v)=>{const el=$(id);if(el)el.textContent=String(v);};
const svgLine=(x1,y1,x2,y2,cls='w10-axis')=>`<line x1="${x1}" y1="${y1}" x2="${x2}" y2="${y2}" class="${cls}"></line>`;
const svgPath=(pts,cls)=>`<path class="${cls}" d="${pts.map((p,i)=>`${i?'L':'M'}${p[0].toFixed(2)},${p[1].toFixed(2)}`).join(' ')}"></path>`;
const txt=(x,y,string,cls='w10-tick',anchor='middle')=>`<text x="${x}" y="${y}" text-anchor="${anchor}" class="${cls}">${string}</text>`;
const pct=p=>Number.isFinite(p)?(100*p).toFixed(1)+'%':'—';
const fixed=(x,d=2)=>Number.isNaN(x)?'—':x===Infinity?'∞':x===-Infinity?'−∞':Number.isFinite(x)?x.toFixed(d):'—';
const safe=(a,b)=>b===0?NaN:a/b;
const axes=(L,R,T,B,xlabels,ylabels)=>{
 let s=svgLine(L,B,R,B)+svgLine(L,T,L,B);
 for(const [v,x] of xlabels)s+=svgLine(x,B,x,B+6)+txt(x,B+26,v);
 for(const [v,y] of ylabels)s+=svgLine(L,y,R,y,'w10-gridline')+txt(L-10,y+5,v,'w10-tick','end');
 return s;
};

/* --------------------------------------------------------
   Diagnostic 5 × 6 display
   -------------------------------------------------------- */
function renderConfusion(){
 const tp=Math.max(0,Math.floor(N('cmTP',0))),fn=Math.max(0,Math.floor(N('cmFN',0)));
 const fp=Math.max(0,Math.floor(N('cmFP',0))),tn=Math.max(0,Math.floor(N('cmTN',0)));
 const sick=tp+fn,healthy=tn+fp,pos=tp+fp,neg=tn+fn,total=sick+healthy;
 const sen=safe(tp,sick),spec=safe(tn,healthy),ppv=safe(tp,pos),npv=safe(tn,neg);
 const fpr=safe(fp,healthy),fnr=safe(fn,sick),fdr=safe(fp,pos),forate=safe(fn,neg);
 const acc=safe(tp+tn,total),bacc=(sen+spec)/2;
 const f1=safe(2*tp,2*tp+fp+fn),fowl= Math.sqrt(ppv*sen);
 const inf=sen+spec-1,marked=ppv+npv-1;
 const mcc=safe(tp*tn-fp*fn,Math.sqrt(pos*sick*healthy*neg));
 const lrp=safe(sen,fpr),lrm=safe(fnr,spec),dor=safe(lrp,lrm);
 const prevTh=safe(Math.sqrt(fpr),Math.sqrt(sen)+Math.sqrt(fpr));
 const jacc=safe(tp,tp+fp+fn);
 out('cmSensBig',pct(sen));out('cmSpecBig',pct(spec));out('cmPpvBig',pct(ppv));out('cmNpvBig',pct(npv));
 // Exactly 5 columns × 6 rows, ordered like the course outline.
 const specs=[
  [['Total',total,'n'],['Healthy',healthy,'n'],['Sick',sick,'n'],['Prevalence',safe(sick,total),'pct'],['Accuracy',acc,'pct'],['Balanced accuracy',bacc,'pct']],
  [['Positive',pos,'n'],['TP',tp,'n'],['FP',fp,'n'],['PPV',ppv,'pct'],['False discovery rate',fdr,'pct'],['F1 score',f1,'decimal']],
  [['Negative',neg,'n'],['FN',fn,'n'],['TN',tn,'n'],['False omission rate',forate,'pct'],['NPV',npv,'pct'],['Fowlkes–Mallows',fowl,'decimal']],
  [['Informedness',inf,'decimal'],['Sensitivity / recall',sen,'pct'],['FPR / fall-out',fpr,'pct'],['LR+',lrp,'decimal'],['Markedness',marked,'decimal'],['Matthews (MCC)',mcc,'decimal']],
  [['Prev. threshold',prevTh,'pct'],['FNR / miss rate',fnr,'pct'],['Specificity',spec,'pct'],['LR−',lrm,'decimal'],['Diagnostic OR',dor,'decimal'],['Jaccard / threat',jacc,'decimal']]
 ];
 const fmt=(v,type)=>type==='n'?String(v):type==='pct'?pct(v):fixed(v,2);
 // Style mapping for matrix categories
 const styleMap = {
   'Healthy': 'model', 'Sick': 'model',
   'Positive': 'observed', 'Negative': 'observed',
   'TP': 'uncertainty', 'TN': 'uncertainty', 'FP': 'uncertainty', 'FN': 'uncertainty',
   'Sensitivity / recall': 'primary', 'Specificity': 'primary', 'PPV': 'primary', 'NPV': 'primary',
   'Balanced accuracy': 'primary', 'Accuracy': 'primary'
 };
 <!-- const el = $('cmMetrics'); -->
 <!-- if (el) el.innerHTML = specs.map(column => -->
 <!--   '<div class="w10-metric-col">' + column.map(([name, value, type]) => -->
 <!--     `<div class="w10-metric ${styleMap[name] || ''}"><strong>${name}</strong><span>${fmt(value, type)}</span></div>`).join('') + '</div>').join(''); -->
 // Formula lookup for tooltip popups
  const formulaMap = {
    'Prevalence': 'Sick / Total',
    'Accuracy': '(TP + TN) / Total',
    'Balanced accuracy': '(Sensitivity + Specificity) / 2',
    'PPV': 'TP / (TP + FP)',
    'False discovery rate': 'FP / (TP + FP)',
    'F1 score': '2·TP / (2·TP + FP + FN)',
    'False omission rate': 'FN / (TN + FN)',
    'NPV': 'TN / (TN + FN)',
    'Fowlkes–Mallows': '√(PPV × Sensitivity)',
    'Informedness': 'Sensitivity + Specificity − 1',
    'Sensitivity / recall': 'TP / (TP + FN)',
    'FPR / fall-out': 'FP / (TN + FP)',
    'LR+': 'Sensitivity / FPR',
    'Markedness': 'PPV + NPV − 1',
    'Matthews (MCC)': '(TP·TN − FP·FN) / √((TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN))',
    'Prev. threshold': '√FPR / (√Sensitivity + √FPR)',
    'FNR / miss rate': 'FN / (TP + FN)',
    'Specificity': 'TN / (TN + FP)',
    'LR−': 'FNR / Specificity',
    'Diagnostic OR': 'LR+ / LR−',
    'Jaccard / threat': 'TP / (TP + FP + FN)'
  };

  const el = $('cmMetrics');
  if (el) el.innerHTML = specs.map(column => 
    '<div class="w10-metric-col">' + column.map(([name, value, type]) => {
      const f = formulaMap[name];
      const tipAttr = f ? ` data-formula="${f}"` : '';
      return `<div class="w10-metric ${styleMap[name] || ''}"${tipAttr}><strong>${name}</strong><span>${fmt(value, type)}</span></div>`;
    }).join('') + '</div>'
  ).join('');
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------
   Diagnostic biomarker + receiver operating characteristic.
   LOW biomarker value is defined as test-positive in BOTH
   synthetic datasets. Sample and ROC remain fixed as slider moves.
   -------------------------------------------------------- */
const markerCache={};
function makeRng(seed){let state=seed>>>0;return ()=>{state^=state<<13;state^=state>>>17;state^=state<<5;return ((state>>>0)+.5)/4294967296;};}
function normalDraw(rand){return Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(Math.max(1e-12,rand())))*Math.cos(2*Math.PI*rand());}
function genMarker(which){
 const rand=makeRng(which==='ferritin'?640091:94741);
 const max=which==='ferritin'?110:22, healthy=[],sick=[];
 for(let i=0;i<72;i++){
  const mh=which==='ferritin'?62:11.1,sh=which==='ferritin'?19:3.2;
  const ms=which==='ferritin'?24:9.9,ss=which==='ferritin'?14:3.6;
  healthy.push(clamp(mh+normalDraw(rand)*sh,.5,max-.5));
  sick.push(clamp(ms+normalDraw(rand)*ss,.5,max-.5));
 }
 return {max,healthy,sick,unit:which==='ferritin'?'ng/mL':'ng/mL'};
}
function markerRates(data,cut){
 const tp=data.sick.filter(v=>v<=cut).length,fn=data.sick.length-tp;
 const fp=data.healthy.filter(v=>v<=cut).length,tn=data.healthy.length-fp;
 return {tp,fn,fp,tn,tpr:tp/data.sick.length,fpr:fp/data.healthy.length};
}
function markerCurve(data){
 const sorted=[...data.healthy,...data.sick].sort((a,b)=>a-b);
 const cuts=[-1,...sorted, data.max+1];
 const seen=new Set(),points=[];let bestCut=0,bestJ=-Infinity;
 for(const c of cuts){if(seen.has(c))continue;seen.add(c);
  const r=markerRates(data,c);points.push({x:r.fpr,y:r.tpr,cut:c});
  const J=r.tpr-r.fpr;if(J>bestJ){bestJ=J;bestCut=c;}
 }
 points.sort((a,b)=>a.x-b.x || a.y-b.y);
 // AUC: U statistic, disease values are positive on the low end.
 let wins=0;
 for(const s of data.sick)for(const h of data.healthy)wins+=s<h?1:s===h?.5:0;
 const auc=wins/(data.sick.length*data.healthy.length);
 return {points,auc,bestCut};
}
function changeMarker(){
 const which=$('rocMarker').value;
 const data=markerCache[which]||(markerCache[which]=genMarker(which));
 const slider=$('rocCut');slider.max=String(data.max);slider.min='0';slider.step=which==='ferritin'?'1':'.2';slider.value=which==='ferritin'?'30':'10';
 renderRoc();
}
function renderRoc(){
 const which=$('rocMarker')?.value||'ferritin',data=markerCache[which]||(markerCache[which]=genMarker(which));
 const cut=N('rocCut',30),scores=markerCurve(data),current=markerRates(data,cut);
 out('rocCutVal',cut.toFixed(which==='ferritin'?0:1)+' '+data.unit);
 out('rocSen',pct(current.tpr));out('rocSpe',pct(1-current.fpr));out('rocAuc',scores.auc.toFixed(3));out('rocBest',scores.bestCut.toFixed(1)+' '+data.unit);
 const svg=$('rocSvg');if(!svg)return;
 const L=66,R=495,T=78,B=372,L2=610,R2=845,T2=91,B2=333;
 const mx=x=>L+x/data.max*(R-L),rX=x=>L2+x*(R2-L2),rY=y=>B2-y*(B2-T2);
 let h=`<defs><clipPath id="w10RocClip"><rect x="${L}" y="${T}" width="${R-L}" height="${B-T}"></rect></clipPath></defs>`;
 h+=`<rect x="${L}" y="${T}" width="${mx(cut)-L}" height="${B-T}" class="w10-hist-selected"></rect>`;
 h+=txt(L,34,'Biomarker values by reference group','w10-svg-title','start')+txt(L2,34,'Receiver operating characteristic','w10-svg-title','start');
 h+=svgLine(L,B,R,B)+svgLine(L,T,L,B)+svgLine(L2,B2,R2,B2)+svgLine(L2,T2,L2,B2);
 for(const f of [0,.25,.5,.75,1]){
   const x=rX(f),y=rY(f);
   h+=svgLine(x,B2,x,B2+6)+txt(x,B2+25,f.toFixed(2));
   h+=svgLine(L2,y,R2,y,'w10-gridline')+txt(L2-8,y+5,f.toFixed(2),'w10-tick','end');
 }
 for(let i=0;i<=5;i++){const v=i/5*data.max;h+=svgLine(mx(v),B,mx(v),B+6)+txt(mx(v),B+25,v.toFixed(which==='ferritin'?0:1));}
 h+=txt((L+R)/2,B+57,which==='ferritin'?'Ferritin (ng/mL)':'Folate (ng/mL)','w10-svg-label');
 h+=txt((L2+R2)/2,B2+58,'False positive rate (1 − Specificity)','w10-svg-label');
 <!-- h+=txt(L2-36,(T2+B2)/2,'True positive rate (Sensitivity)','w10-svg-label'); -->
 const yX = L2 - 45, yY = (T2 + B2) / 2;
 h += `<text x="${yX}" y="${yY}" transform="rotate(-90, ${yX}, ${yY})" text-anchor="middle" class="w10-svg-label">True positive rate (Sensitivity)</text>`;
 h+=txt(L+6,116,'Healthy · blue','w10-svg-label','start');h+=txt(L+6,266,'Sick · orange','w10-svg-label','start');
 const rand=makeRng(97621);let dots='';
 for(const [className,values,y] of [['w10-healthy',data.healthy,164],['w10-sick',data.sick,315]]){
   for(const v of values){const yy=y+(rand()-.5)*75;
    dots+=`<circle cx="${mx(v).toFixed(2)}" cy="${yy.toFixed(2)}" r="4.0" class="${className}"></circle>`;}
 }
 h+=`<g clip-path="url(#w10RocClip)">${dots}${svgLine(mx(cut),T,mx(cut),B,'w10-marker-line')}</g>`;
 h+=txt(clamp(mx(cut)+9,L+20,R-20),T+25,'cutoff','w10-svg-muted','start');
 h+=svgLine(L2,B2,R2,T2,'w10-gridline');
 h+=svgPath(scores.points.map(p=>[rX(p.x),rY(p.y)]),'w10-roc-line');
 const br=markerRates(data,scores.bestCut);
 h+=`<circle cx="${rX(br.fpr)}" cy="${rY(br.tpr)}" r="6" fill="#18864b" stroke="white" stroke-width="2"></circle>`;
 h+=`<circle cx="${rX(current.fpr)}" cy="${rY(current.tpr)}" r="8" class="w10-roc-dot"></circle>`;
 h+=txt(R2,60,`AUC ${scores.auc.toFixed(3)} · sample Youden max marked in green`,'w10-svg-muted','end');
 svg.innerHTML=h;
}
let rocDrag=false;
function rocPointer(event){
 const svg=$('rocSvg');if(!svg)return;
 const ctm=svg.getScreenCTM();if(!ctm)return;
 const loc=new DOMPoint(event.clientX,event.clientY).matrixTransform(ctm.inverse());
 const which=$('rocMarker').value,data=markerCache[which];
 const L=66,R=495,T=78,B=372;
 if(loc.x<L-15||loc.x>R+15||loc.y<T-15||loc.y>B+15)return;
 const value=clamp((loc.x-L)/(R-L)*data.max,0,data.max);
 const step=which==='ferritin'?1:.2;
 $('rocCut').value=String(Math.round(value/step)*step);
 renderRoc();
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------
   Sequential randomization. Mode only alters next assignment.
   No clinical outcome information is ever used.
   -------------------------------------------------------- */
let randState=90418, allocations=[];
function randomU(){randState^=randState<<13;randState^=randState>>>17;randState^=randState<<5;return ((randState>>>0)+.5)/4294967296;}
function assignmentProb(){const t=allocations.filter(x=>x===1).length,c=allocations.length-t;
 if($('ranMode')?.value!=='biased'||t===c)return .5;
 return t<c?.75:.25;
}
function assignPatients(n){for(let i=0;i<n;i++){const p=assignmentProb();allocations.push(randomU()<p?1:0);}renderRandom();}
function renderRandom(){
 const t=allocations.filter(x=>x===1).length,c=allocations.length-t;
 out('ranCounts',`${t} / ${c}`);out('ranProbability',assignmentProb().toFixed(2));out('ranTotal',allocations.length);out('ranGap',Math.abs(t-c));
 const svg=$('randomSvg');if(!svg)return;
 let h=txt(60,35,'Allocations in arrival order','w10-svg-title','start')+txt(495,35,'Accumulated arm balance','w10-svg-title','start');
 h+=`<rect x="60" y="60" width="395" height="330" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#d9e1ea"></rect>`;
 const boxes=allocations.slice(-120);
 boxes.forEach((v,i)=>{const col=i%15,row=Math.floor(i/15);h+=`<rect x="${70+col*25.5}" y="${70+row*36.5}" width="20.5" height="24" rx="4" class="${v?'w10-ranT':'w10-ranC'}"></rect>`;});
 h+=txt(62,420,'Last 120 assignments · green treatment / blue control','w10-svg-muted','start');
 const L=525,R=850,T=88,B=374;h+=svgLine(L,B,R,B)+svgLine(L,T,L,B);
 const maxN=Math.max(20,allocations.length);const maxIm=Math.max(4,Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(Math.max(1,allocations.length))*2));
 const mx=i=>L+i/maxN*(R-L),my=v=>(B+T)/2-v/maxIm*(B-T)/2;
 h+=svgLine(L,my(0),R,my(0),'w10-gridline');
 for(const v of [-maxIm,0,maxIm])h+=txt(L-10,my(v)+5,v,'w10-tick','end');
 for(const i of [0,.25,.5,.75,1])h+=txt(mx(i*maxN),B+25,Math.round(i*maxN));
 if(allocations.length){let bal=0;const coords=[[mx(0),my(0)]];
   for(let i=0;i<allocations.length;i++){bal+=allocations[i]?1:-1;coords.push([mx(i+1),my(clamp(bal,-maxIm,maxIm))]);}
   h+=svgPath(coords,'w10-power-line');
   h+=`<circle cx="${mx(allocations.length)}" cy="${my(clamp(bal,-maxIm,maxIm))}" r="6" fill="#c93838"></circle>`;
 }
 h+=txt(695,447,'Treatment − control assignment count','w10-svg-muted');
 svg.innerHTML=h;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------
   Planning calculator: t-critical from finite-df expansion;
   power under a normal approximation to noncentral-t power.
   Explicitly described as approximate on the slide.
   -------------------------------------------------------- */
function normCdf(x){
 // Hastings polynomial (absolute error near 1e-7 for N(0,1)).
 const t=1/(1+0.2316419*Math.abs(x));
 const d=0.3989422804014327*Math.exp(-x*x/2);
 const tail=d*t*(0.319381530+t*(-0.356563782+t*(1.781477937+t*(-1.821255978+t*1.330274429))));
 return x>=0?1-tail:tail;
}
function normInv(p){
 // Acklam rational approximation; all caller p are strictly between zero and one.
 const a=[-39.6968302866538,220.946098424521,-275.928510446969,138.357751867269,-30.6647980661472,2.50662827745924];
 const b=[-54.4760987982241,161.585836858041,-155.698979859887,66.8013118877197,-13.2806815528857];
 const c=[-0.00778489400243029,-0.322396458041136,-2.40075827716184,-2.54973253934373,4.37466414146497,2.93816398269878];
 const d=[0.00778469570904146,0.32246712907004,2.445134137143,3.75440866190742];
 if(p<.02425){const q=Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(p));return (((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5])/((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1);}
 if(p>1-.02425)return -normInv(1-p);
 const q=p-.5,r=q*q;
 return (((((a[0]*r+a[1])*r+a[2])*r+a[3])*r+a[4])*r+a[5])*q/(((((b[0]*r+b[1])*r+b[2])*r+b[3])*r+b[4])*r+1);
}
function approxTCrit(p,df){const z=normInv(p),z2=z*z,z3=z*z2,z5=z3*z2,z7=z5*z2;
 return z+(z3+z)/(4*df)+(5*z5+16*z3+3*z)/(96*df*df)+(3*z7+19*z5+17*z3-15*z)/(384*df*df*df);
}
function approxPower(n,delta,sd,alpha){
 if(n<2)return 0;
 const ncp=Math.abs(delta)/(sd*Math.sqrt(2/n)),crit=approxTCrit(1-alpha/2,2*n-2);
 return clamp(1-normCdf(crit-ncp)+normCdf(-crit-ncp),0,1);
}
function renderPower(){
 const delta=Math.abs(N('powEffect',5)),sd=N('powSd',12),alpha=N('powAlpha',.05),target=N('powTarget',.8);
 if(!(sd>0&&delta>0)){
 for(const id of ['powN','powTotal','powD','powAttained'])out(id,'—');out('powNote','Enter positive anticipated effect and SD.');$('powerSvg').innerHTML='';return;
 }
 const MAX=20000;let targetN=null;
 for(let n=2;n<=MAX;n++){if(approxPower(n,delta,sd,alpha)>=target){targetN=n;break;}}
 const shown=targetN||MAX;
 out('powN',targetN?shown.toLocaleString():'>20,000');out('powTotal',targetN?(shown*2).toLocaleString():'>40,000');out('powD',(delta/sd).toFixed(2));
 out('powAttained',targetN?pct(approxPower(shown,delta,sd,alpha)):'< target by 20,000');
 out('powNote',targetN?'Approximate t-test power using a finite-df t critical value and normal tail approximation; no dropout adjustment.':'Required n exceeds the displayed search limit; investigate feasibility and assumptions.');
 const svg=$('powerSvg');if(!svg)return;
 const L=85,R=854,T=58,B=375,maxN=Math.max(40,Math.min(2000,Math.round(shown*1.35)));
 const mx=n=>L+(n-2)/(maxN-2)*(R-L),my=p=>B-(p-.0)*(B-T);
 let h=axes(L,R,T,B,[[2,mx(2)],[Math.round(maxN/4),mx(maxN/4)],[Math.round(maxN/2),mx(maxN/2)],[Math.round(maxN*3/4),mx(maxN*3/4)],[maxN,mx(maxN)]],[[0,my(0)],[.25,my(.25)],[.5,my(.5)],[.75,my(.75)],[1,my(1)]]);
 h+=txt(L,28,'Planning power vs patients per arm','w10-svg-title','start');
 h+=svgLine(L,my(target),R,my(target),'w10-marker-line');
 const pts=Array.from({length:220},(_,i)=>{const n=2+(maxN-2)*i/219;return[mx(n),my(approxPower(n,delta,sd,alpha))];});
 h+=svgPath(pts,'w10-power-line');
 if(targetN&&targetN<=maxN){h+=svgLine(mx(shown),my(0),mx(shown),my(target),'w10-marker-line');
 h+=`<circle cx="${mx(shown)}" cy="${my(approxPower(shown,delta,sd,alpha))}" r="8" class="w10-power-dot"></circle>`;}
 h+=txt((L+R)/2,443,'Patients per arm (equal allocation)','w10-svg-label');h+=txt(R,36,`Target ${Math.round(target*100)}% · two-sided α = ${alpha}`,'w10-svg-muted','end');
 svg.innerHTML=h;
}

const quizAnswers={
 '1':['C','NPV = TN / (TN + FN); the denominator includes all negative test results.'],
 '2':['B','A cutoff changes sensitivity and specificity. The AUC for fixed biomarker scores remains constant.'],
 '3':['C','Randomization removes systematic assignment mechanisms on average, not random variation.'],
 '4':['A','Between-study differences require inspection of heterogeneity, bias and applicability.']
};
function answerQuiz(button){
 const card=button.closest('.w10-quiz'),spec=quizAnswers[card?.dataset.quiz];if(!spec)return;
 const correct=button.dataset.choice===spec[0];
 card.querySelectorAll('.w10-choice').forEach(b=>b.classList.remove('correct','wrong'));
 button.classList.add(correct?'correct':'wrong');
 const el=card.querySelector('.w10-quiz-feedback');if(el){el.className='w10-quiz-feedback '+(correct?'correct':'wrong');el.textContent=(correct?'Correct. ':'Not quite. ')+spec[1];}
}

let initialized=false;
function initWeek10(){
 if(initialized||!$('confWidget'))return;
 initialized=true;
 for(const id of ['cmTP','cmFN','cmFP','cmTN'])$(id)?.addEventListener('input',renderConfusion);
 $('rocMarker')?.addEventListener('change',changeMarker);
 $('rocCut')?.addEventListener('input',renderRoc);
 const rs=$('rocSvg');
 rs?.addEventListener('pointerdown',e=>{const ctm=rs.getScreenCTM();if(!ctm)return;const p=new DOMPoint(e.clientX,e.clientY).matrixTransform(ctm.inverse());
  if(p.x>=51&&p.x<=510&&p.y>=65&&p.y<=395){rocDrag=true;rs.setPointerCapture?.(e.pointerId);rocPointer(e);}
 });
 rs?.addEventListener('pointermove',e=>{if(rocDrag)rocPointer(e);});
 rs?.addEventListener('pointerup',()=>{rocDrag=false;});
 rs?.addEventListener('pointercancel',()=>{rocDrag=false;});
 $('ranOne')?.addEventListener('click',()=>assignPatients(1));
 $('ranTen')?.addEventListener('click',()=>assignPatients(10));
 $('ranReset')?.addEventListener('click',()=>{allocations=[];randState=90418;renderRandom();});
 $('ranMode')?.addEventListener('change',renderRandom);
 for(const id of ['powEffect','powSd','powAlpha','powTarget'])$(id)?.addEventListener('input',renderPower);
 document.querySelectorAll('.w10-choice').forEach(b=>b.addEventListener('click',()=>answerQuiz(b)));
 renderConfusion();changeMarker();renderRandom();renderPower();
}
if(document.readyState==='loading')document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',initWeek10);else initWeek10();
window.addEventListener('load',initWeek10);
if(window.Reveal&&typeof window.Reveal.on==='function'){
 window.Reveal.on('ready',initWeek10);window.Reveal.on('slidechanged',initWeek10);
}
})();

</script>
